name: Trans-New Guinea Family

linguisticChallenges.medialVerbs: Trans-New Guinea languages widely use medial verb forms in clause chains — sequences of dependent clauses marked for same-subject or different-subject relative to the following clause. This switch-reference system has no parallel in most target languages.
linguisticChallenges.agglutination: Most members are agglutinative with SOV word order. Verb-final structure is consistent across the family.

notes: Minimal family card for Trans-New Guinea (~312 members). One of the largest language families but with limited shared properties documented for translation purposes. Members are spread across the highlands of New Guinea. SOV word order and medial verb/switch-reference systems are the most consistently shared features.
